answer: Cross-Epoch Behaviour Thread Matching. Each identity’s action sequence is hashed into a per-epoch thread; a new epoch is accepted only if its thread overlaps the prior epoch on a shared behavioural ledge of at least k recurring task signatures. Sybils splitting into fresh identities break continuity and fail the overlap check. Attackers must maintain consistent costly behaviour across epochs, paying repeated execution and storage costs per identity, which scales linearly and makes mass fabrication uneconomical. An ivory audit log retains the proofs.
